boundary.title: Harness
boundary.summary: The caller-neutral Agent execution boundary for immutable Run attempts, privacy-bounded durable continuity, Provider and Tool recovery, receipts, and completion proposals.
boundary.thesis: One bounded Agent Run may be replaced without becoming the owner of durable work or caller-domain truth.
boundary.question: Which Run-local facts must survive interruption while execution policy and Task meaning remain outside the Harness authority?
boundary: No final caller or domain authority

project.label: Caller-neutral Agent execution
project.problem: Agent execution needs durable Run-local authority and recovery without making a Provider session, Host, or caller-domain state the owner of the Run.
project.capability: Compiles caller-delegated execution mandates and exact Run contracts into bounded Agent attempts with durable Provider/Tool recovery, Agent-selected cognition, request-bound action authority, optional bounded ToolProgram composition, pause/resume, receipts, and caller-defined structured completion whose local structural conformance can be verified without taking semantic completion authority from the caller/domain.
project.audience: Agent builders who need caller-neutral Run execution, bounded authority, explicit Provider and Tool recovery, and completion handoff without a Host dependency.
project.latestProof: At the current public-source revision, opt-in local JSON-Schema structural conformance rejects schema-invalid Provider completion output before candidate completion while leaving semantic/evidence admission with the caller or domain. This closes a concrete control-boundary failure without turning Harness into domain truth authority.
project.summary: The independent execution authority for bounded Agent Runs. Harness owns how an admitted attempt executes and what Run content it may durably retain, while callers retain Task meaning, domain commitments, and final verification.
project.state: Operational pre-1.0 for caller-neutral independent Runs. Harness separates canonical history, Agent-selected durable cognition, interaction/attempt cognition, installed versus Run/turn-admitted capabilities, Tool effect recovery, and optional local structured-result conformance. Advanced ToolProgram and cross-Run exact-reference paths remain bounded mechanisms rather than automatic authority or semantic policy.
